root.name: Ruy Lopez: Bird Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nd4

overview: Black plants a knight on d4 at once. The normal reply is 4.Nxd4 exd4 5.O-O or 5.d3 c6 6.Ba4, after which Black has a cramping pawn on d4 and gains space, while White keeps the bishop pair-ish play and central e4 control. 4.Bc4 is a more direct alternative. The game is manoeuvring, with Black's d4 pawn both a strength and a target.

white_ideas.idea: Capture on d4 and play d3 or O-O, then attack the d4 pawn with c3
Retreat the bishop to a4 or c4 and keep a sound game
Open the position with c3 or f4 to exploit Black's loosened kingside

black_ideas.idea: Gain space with the d4 pawn and play ...c6, ...Bc5, ...Ne7
Hold the d4 pawn and develop with ...d6 and ...Nf6
Use the half-open e-file and central space for kingside play

typical_structures.structure: Black pawn on d4 against White pawn on e4 with a semi-closed centre

character.notes: Slow positional game after the trade on d4; neither side gets forcing play.

soundness.notes: Playable for Black; White keeps a small edge but there is no refutation.

structure.notes: Black d4 pawn against e4 gives a semi-fixed centre; flexible.

level.notes: Positional manoeuvring on a fixed centre.

sublines_that_differ.name: 4.Bc4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nd4 4. Bc4
sublines_that_differ.how: Avoids the trade and aims at f7, sharper and trickier.

character.reason: Neither forcing nor especially solid after 4.Nxd4 exd4.

soundness.reason: Slightly worse for Black but playable.

structure.reason: d4 vs e4 with tension, undecided.

plans.reason: Black gains space with the d4 pawn.
